Nebius Secures $3.5 Billion From Citi as It Shifts From Converts to Secured Debt ©Scharfsinn86 from Getty Images and luthfil aziman effendi from Gambar Luthfil aziman effendi via Canva
Key Takeaways

Nebius secured a $3.5 billion senior secured facility from Citi on October 22, its second contract-backed financing since July.

Q2 revenue rose 454% to $582.3 million, but the $7 billion to $9 billion run-rate target implies a steep second-half ramp.

Roughly $10 billion of convertible debt and a 364-day maturity on the new facility keep refinancing risk front and center.

The November 12 Q3 report, with consensus revenue near $905 million, will test how quickly contracts turn into revenue.

Nebius Group (NBIS:NASDAQ) has found a new way to pay for its buildout. Instead of selling another convertible, it is borrowing against the customers it already signed.

The company secured a $3.5 billion senior secured facility from Citigroup (C:NYSE) on October 22. Shares still fell 6.8% last week to $159, caught in a neocloud selloff tied to AI debt fears.

That leaves the stock about 47% below its $299.86 high, even though Street targets average $281.

I find the financing shift more interesting than the headline number. It changes who bears the risk if the buildout slips.

A one-year loan for long assets

The Citi deal has three features worth noting:

A 364-day maturity, so it functions as bridge capital

Pricing at Term SOFR plus 2.75%, stepping up to a maximum of 3.50%

Proceeds aimed at data center development, GPU procurement and general corporate purposes

It follows Nebius's first secured facility, a $775 million loan in July priced at SOFR plus 2.50% and maturing in 2030. Deployed GPUs and contracted cash flows from an investment-grade customer back that one.

Before July, convertibles did most of the work. Nebius closed $5.75 billion of notes in August, leaving roughly $10 billion of convertible debt outstanding.

So how much debt has the balance sheet absorbed so far?

Nebius Group (NBIS): total debt, quarterly, $ billions, Q2 2025–Q2 2026 (TIKR)

Total debt stepped up sharply in 2026, and the Citi facility adds to that before any refinancing.

Contracts doing the collateral work

The pitch to lenders rests on more than $40 billion of long-term contracts with investment-grade customers, including Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ) and Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ). Those contracts can serve as collateral for future asset-backed deals.

Growth gives the strategy credibility. Q2 revenue rose 454% to $582.3 million, and first-half revenue reached $981.3 million, up 529%.

New channels keep arriving, too. A $1 billion-plus compute deal with Reflection runs through 2029, and a partnership with Palantir Technologies (PLTR:NASDAQ) adds a sovereign AI channel for government and enterprise buyers.

What Happened?

China's securities regulator approved Citigroup's (C:NYSE) plan for a fully owned securities company on October 23, Citi said in a press release. Citi applied in late 2021. Reports in May said the application had cleared review, so the October 23 decision formalizes an expected approval.

The Shanghai-based unit can offer equities brokerage, underwriting, research and principal trading onshore. It still has to complete remaining regulatory and statutory steps before opening, and Citi gave no start date. The stock closed October 22 at $122.51, 15.90% below its one-year peak on TIKR's drawdown chart, and trades at about 10 times forward earnings.

Citigroup Drawdowns (TIKR)
A Late Entry Into China That Builds on Citi's Asia Gains

JPMorgan Chase (JPM) and Goldman Sachs (GS) won approval to fully own their China securities firms in 2021. According to their China annual reports, as cited by Reuters, Goldman's unit earned about $217 million in 2025 and JPMorgan's earned 984 million yuan. Citi reported $5.2 billion of net income in the third quarter alone, so the new unit will not move near-term earnings.

Its value lies in how it extends an existing push. On the October 13 call, Chair and CEO Jane Fraser said equities revenue rose 14% year over year, "driven by our performance in prime and in Asia, where we have been investing to gain share." She also cited Citi leading SK hynix's offering, which she called the largest-ever IPO by an Asian-based issuer.

AI Is Already Cutting Citi's Costs

Since June 30, Wall Street's next-twelve-month normalized EPS estimate for Citi has risen from $11.23 to $12.28, while the stock fell from $139.96 to $122.51. Part of that rise comes from the 12-month window rolling toward 2027, when analysts expect normalized EPS of around $13, up from around $11 in 2026.

Citigroup EPS Normalized (TIKR)

Fraser tied part of that earnings path to AI. She said tech vendor spend fell 30% year over year as 14,000 engineers used the coding tool Devin to bring work in-house, and "that's still got a long way to run." She added that AI and automation benefits "significantly outweigh the investments we've made year-to-date." Management still guides to a full-year efficiency ratio below 60%.

Not everything points up. Management expects fourth-quarter Markets revenue to drop around 20% or more from the third quarter. The Street's mean target has also slipped, from $154.90 on September 30 to $151.00.

What Happened?

China's securities regulator approved Citi's (C:NYSE) plan to set up a fully owned securities unit in China, Reuters reported on Friday.

It lets the bank grow its presence in the world's second-largest economy.

The unit is called Citigroup Securities China Company and will be based in Shanghai. It can offer onshore capital markets services to local and foreign clients.

These include underwriting, equities brokerage, trading onshore securities, research and investment advice.

Citi applied for this license in late 2021 and has been hiring for the business over the last couple of years.

A person familiar with the matter told Reuters the bank aims to roughly double its team to around 100 people by the end of this year.

CEO Jane Fraser said onshore capabilities will help Citi do more for clients.

That includes raising capital, reaching investors and trading locally, while linking them to global opportunities.

What the Market Is Telling Us About Citigroup Stock

This is a long-awaited approval, not a surprise earnings event. The direct impact on Citigroup stock is likely small for now as the unit is just getting started.

On its Q3 call, Citi said Services revenue rose 15%, and equities revenue rose 14%, helped by growth in Asia, where the bank has been investing to gain share.

Banking revenue grew 6%. Citi also led the SK hynix IPO, the largest-ever IPO of an Asian-based issuer.

Citi earned $5.2 billion in Q3, or $2.85 per share. Revenue was $23.8 billion, up 8%, and return on tangible common equity was 11.5%.

The bank also returned over $4 billion to shareholders, including $3 billion in buybacks.

Management has targets too. Citi expects to beat its 10% to 11% return target this year and aims for 11% to 13% in the near term, and 14% to 15% over time.

However, Jane Fraser said China's economy leans heavily on exports, and Citi is also pulling some investment spending forward, which adds costs.

For Citigroup stock, this approval is one more step in a bigger plan, and investors will likely watch how fast the China unit grows.

Citigroup stock still depends mostly on overall returns, capital, and expense control.

title: Citi closes ‘first-of-its-kind’ $72M bond for biochar project
detail:
Citi closes ‘first-of-its-kind’ $72M bond for biochar project
Citi signage is displayed in Manhattan on March 1, 2024, in New York City. · ESG Dive · Spencer Platt / Staff via Getty Images
Lamar Johnson
Fri, October 23, 2026 at 9:33 AM PDT 3 min read
C
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This story was originally published on ESG Dive. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily ESG Dive newsletter.

Dive Brief:

Citigroup announced this week it had closed a $72 million bond for a biochar carbon removal project, representing a "first-of-its-kind" outcome bond for verified carbon removal, the bank said in a press release. Outcome bonds have returns linked to performance of "predetermined development outcomes," according to the Luxembourg Stock Exchange.

The bond runs for three and a half years and is designed to support carbon removal startup Applied Carbon and its biochar project in Texas. Under the bond, investors will forgo traditional coupon payments and Applied Carbon will receive upfront financing for its project, according to the Wednesday release.

Applied Carbon has at least 198,190 tons of carbon dioxide removals contracted so far, according to carbon dioxide removals registry and data analytics platform CDR.fyi. Microsoft serves as the anchor offtaker for the Texas project, and Citi said in the release that Microsoft's offtake agreement provides "long-term demand support for the underlying carbon removal activity."

Dive Insight:

With investors forgoing traditional payments under the bond, their returns will be linked to the issuance and delivery of carbon credits from Applied Carbon's Texas biochar project, according to the Oct. 21 release. The carbon removal startup creates biochar on the move, with a mobile system designed to pick up crop residue, pyrolyze it and cool the resulting biochar, all while in the field, according to Applied Carbon's website.

The outcome bond issuance looks to build on Citi's work "linking bond performance to environmental outcomes," according to Sonia Battikh, the bank's global head of carbon offsets trading.

"The voluntary carbon market requires new financial structures to bridge the gap between investor capital and the long-term funding needs of carbon removal projects," Battikh said. "By bringing together investors, project developers and long-term carbon demand, we are continuing to expand the range of opportunities through which capital markets can finance real-world outcomes."

Biochar is created by decomposing biomass like food scraps, wood chips or, in this case, crop residue without oxygen. The remainder is a black carbon mineralized substance that can then be mixed with soil to increase its ability to draw down and store carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, according to the U.S. Agricultural Research Service, a branch of the U.S. Department of Agriculture.

Verizon Communications (VZ), T-Mobile US (TMUS) and AT&T (T) stocks came into focus Friday after Citi warned of further valuation pressure on established telecom operators as SpaceX (SPCX) advances plans to enter the U.S. wireless market.

According to a note cited by TheFly, Citi sees 29%-32% valuation risk for the three carriers, with a 4%-16% downside potential from current levels following their pullbacks in 2026.

The firm believes SpaceX is likely to build its own telecommunications company to compete in the U.S. mobile market, rather than become a mobile virtual network operator, an outcome it considers unlikely.

At the time of writing, Verizon (VZ) shares fell more than 1%, while T-Mobile (TMUS) and AT&T (T) declined over 5% each. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was 'bearish' for T-Mobile (TMUS) and Verizon (VZ), while AT&T (T) attracted 'bullish' sentiment.

SpaceX Eyes 80,000 Cell Sites For Nationwide Wireless Network

SpaceX is seeking access to at least 80,000 cell sites across the U.S. and is in discussions with major infrastructure providers, Bloomberg reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The potential leasing agreements, which could be worth billions of dollars, would help SpaceX establish a fourth nationwide wireless carrier to compete with the country's dominant operators, the report said.

SpaceX has also pursued low-band wireless spectrum to complement its Starlink satellites and received Federal Communications Commission approval for 15,000 additional satellites designed to provide mobile service directly to phones.

During SpaceX's earnings call this week, CEO Elon Musk said the company plans to build terrestrial networks to provide broader connectivity wherever SpaceX and Starlink are permitted to operate.

Citi Sees Upside For Tower Operators

While Citi views SpaceX's potential entry as negative for established telecom operators, it considers the reported cell-site plans a net positive for Crown Castle (CCI), SBA Communications (SBAC) and American Tower (AMT).

title: C's September Card Delinquencies Rise: Will This Impact Asset Quality?
detail:
C's September Card Delinquencies Rise: Will This Impact Asset Quality?
Zacks Equity Research
Fri, October 23, 2026 at 5:41 AM PDT 3 min read
C
BAC
JPM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Citigroup Inc. C continues to navigate credit-quality challenges amid an uncertain economic environment. According to its latest SEC filing, its subsidiary, Citibank N.A., reported higher credit card delinquencies and net principal losses in September 2026, while outstanding principal receivables declined during the month.

For the period ended Sept. 25, 2026, the Citibank Credit Card Master Trust I reported principal receivables of $18.7 billion, down from $19.1 billion at the beginning of the period. Receivables delinquent for 30 days or more increased to 1.35% in September from 1.29% in August, while those delinquent for 90 days or more rose to 0.65% from 0.63%. The Citibank Credit Card Issuance Trust's annualized net principal loss rate climbed to 2.18% from 2.03% in August and 1.90% in July, signaling a pickup in credit losses.

The detailed filing also showed that 97.3% of receivables were current in September. However, balances delinquent for 31-60 days were $80.7 million, while those delinquent for 151-180 days totaled $37.4 million. The portfolio's annualized gross yield was 25.03%, while the principal payment rate was 41.45%. Although the high portfolio yield provides a revenue cushion against credit losses, the increase in delinquencies and net principal losses warrants monitoring. These figures relate to the securitized credit card portfolios and should not be interpreted as representing Citigroup's entire loan portfolio.

Citigroup's broader asset-quality picture remains a concern. Although provisions for credit losses declined 2% year over year to $7.91 billion in the first nine months of 2026, the metric recorded a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 24.5% from 2022 to 2025. However, credit quality showed improvement in the third quarter, with the U.S. Cards net credit loss rate declining to 3.6% from 4.0% a year earlier. Management's earlier 2026 guidance projected a U.S. card net credit loss rate of 4-4.5%, highlighting continued credit risks.

Citigroup's organizational overhaul, business simplification initiatives and focus on operational efficiency could support profitability over the longer term. However, persistent inflation, pressure on borrowers' repayment capacity and rising card losses could weigh on asset quality. Any sustained deterioration in credit trends may lead to higher provisions and constrain earnings growth, even as the company benefits from resilient net interest income and a stronger focus on core businesses.

Citigroup (C) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.

Shares of this U.S. bank have returned -7.3% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -1.2% change. The Zacks Financial - Investment Bank industry, to which Citigroup belongs, has lost 5.3% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Citigroup is expected to post earnings of $2.39 per share, indicating a change of +32% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -0.7% over the last 30 days.

The consensus earnings estimate of $11.44 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +43.5%. This estimate has changed +2.1% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $13.1 indicates a change of +14.5% from what Citigroup is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +1.2%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for Citigroup.

Texas Capital Bancshares, Inc. TCBI delivered record revenues of $356.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, up 4.8% year over year. Growth reflected higher net interest income (NII) and higher non-interest income, highlighting the contribution of its lending and fee-generating businesses.

During the quarter, NII rose 1.2% year over year to a record $275 million, supported by higher average earning assets and lower funding costs. Meanwhile, non-interest income climbed 19% to $81.6 million, driven by stronger service charges on deposit accounts, investment banking and advisory fees and trading income. Adding to the positive momentum, fee income from strategic areas of focus reached a quarterly record of $64.1 million, up 14% year over year, reflecting continued strength in investment banking, trading and treasury product fees.

The latest performance builds on TCBI's longer-term growth trajectory. Over the five years ended 2025, its revenues recorded a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 3.6%, while NII and non-interest income expanded at CAGRs of 3.9% and 2.3%, respectively. Although the Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points in September 2026, growth in average earning assets, loan repricing and a favorable loan and deposit mix could support NII. For the fourth quarter of 2026, management projects NII of $270-$275 million compared with $267.4 million in the prior-year quarter.

On the fee-income front, continued investment banking activity, expanding treasury services and wealth management capabilities could support fee-income growth and further diversify revenues. Reflecting these opportunities, non-interest income is projected to reach $70-$75 million in the fourth quarter, up from $60 million in the prior-year quarter.

Supported by its revenue diversification efforts and solid third-quarter performance, TCBI raised its full-year 2026 adjusted total revenue growth guidance to the high-single-digit range from the previously expected mid-to-high-single-digit range. Continued momentum across fee-generating businesses and client acquisition efforts could support this outlook. However, economic uncertainty, higher operating expenses and potential credit-quality pressures remain key risks to sustained growth.

Other Major Banks Deliver Strong Revenue Growth in Q3

U.S. Bancorp USB and Citigroup C also reported strong revenue growth in the third quarter of 2026.

U.S. Bancorp reported record net revenues of $7.97 billion, up 8.7% year over year, driven by growth in NII and fee income, particularly from capital markets, investment management and treasury services.
